Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Yushan. Yushan Shangsi owns the recorded exchange — the birthday claim turned back with what is the affair of your meeting, the lion's-cub boast, and the fine-hand over-praised check.

Senses.Explanation: A courtesy formula of unexpected gain — went out small and met great — supplied at the root by Yunmen for a speechless newcomer, and claimed, graded, denied, staged, and promised across the Song case-halls and the Qing assemblies. The root sits in Yunmen Wenyan's own screening-talk record: a newcomer is asked — on South Peak you borrowed two hundred coins of me; why do you not repay? — and at his silence the master lends him the answer: today I went out small and met great; and again: today the occasion passed me by; Xutang Zhiyu's hall carries the courtesy line live — not only did the great assembly behold the sight; I went out small and met great — and the grading answer lands at once: a thieving-mind little devil; the monk bows, the master raises his staff: were it me, Huqiu come directly down, like a rich heir of many generations not one coin misspent, each life fierce and cramped only because the family discipline is too strict; Dachuan Puji raises Huitang Zuxin's Nanxiong monk — better go home; in your village three coins buy a piece of fish-roe palm-sized — and rules: rather be ground to dust than blind one monk's eyes; Huitang's cooked place unforgotten, but that monk did not know going-out-small-meeting-great — had he known to raise fist and spirit, where in the world was there room for him?; and Shitian Faxun, over the emperor's cloud-rest hermit who came wordless to court with Xuedou's supplied answer — none escapes the perfect transforming — finds Xuedou true to the coming occasion yet still a shrimp that cannot leap out: were I the new abbot, I would have answered then: today I went out small and met great — does it still meet the sagely intent? a long stillness, then: used to passing before the five-phoenix tower, hand on the golden whip, hailing the great peace. Shending Yikui raises the scholar with the Thousand-Buddha Name Sutra — a hundred thousand buddhas seen by name only, what land do they dwell in, do they convert beings? — and Changsha Jingcen's return: since Cui Hao inscribed the poem on Yellow Crane Tower, has the scholar inscribed one? not yet — then find leisure to set down a good one; Yikui rules the old great teacher well met the coming impulse, yet imposed on another what he himself would not wish; the scholar went out small and met great, how it outdoes the airs — and yet his nostrils remain in another man's hands; setting that aside: does the assembly want to know the going-out-small-meeting-great affair? without the connoisseur's eye of Zhonglang, it is still firewood at a rustic shed; Yuan'an Liao, in an address of praise where the buddhas cannot speak it, the founding teachers cannot lift it, the ten great commentators cannot annotate it, the world's patch-robed ones cannot reach it — heaven and earth not vast enough, sun and moon not bright enough, the hungry fed and the sick righted — widens the promise past all courtesy: making everyone come empty and return full, setting each and all to go out small and meet great, the three wretched roads turned to level highways and the six desires' turning wheel stilled; and Yushan Shangsi, at the birthday seat his senior monks and the mountain elders beg him to take, hears the claim from the asking monk — today I too go out small and meet great — and turns it back: what is the affair of your meeting? the monk answers with the hero's line — to stand out from the herd one must be a bold spirit; to win the field, a lion's cub — and the master checks the boasting: a fine hand, over-praised.
